account:
Today my ordinary appointments continue: the mill inspection at ten, lunch at home, council letters, tea with my neighbour at three, and office business later. The unusual event is an eighteen hundred to eighteen thirty civic presentation in the great hall. The innkeeper requested it, I approved it, and the secretary recorded a signed supplement. It explicitly asks me to arrive precisely at six, not earlier, so the organisers can finish preparations around their work. I heard the secretary promise to keep its contents private. The stated subject is appreciation of municipal public service from the inn and local tradespeople. This makes me suspect a surprise celebration or tribute, possibly for me, rather than ordinary public business, though I do not know the actual contents.

There are also repeated, rather vague reports of a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery. A townsman named baker and innkeeper, builder and innkeeper, and baker, freight and neighbour as having been there. Yesterday I personally saw the builder give the baker oak planks and a lantern. Those supplies and the gatherings could relate to preparations, or to genuine riverside improvements; I cannot yet establish which. My neighbour says she is gathering suggestions and will discuss them at tea. Freight specifically proposed lighting both ferry landings and marking safe waiting areas away from the water, and the secretary acknowledged those suggestions. Those are concrete safety proposals, unlike the vague bakery rumours. I have asked that they be noted. I am now at the mill for my scheduled inspection, but have not yet found anyone who has provided a grain report.
